question: Should OpenClaw accept `currentTokenCount` plus these SDK token-budget helpers as the stable public ContextEngine/plugin SDK contract now, or fold this signal into the broader assemble metadata design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82137?
rationale: This is an additive but public plugin API contract that third-party context-engine authors may compile against, and a related RFC is still open for the same assemble surface.

options.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Proof
options.body: Approve `currentTokenCount` as a standalone assemble signal, then require SDK baseline regeneration and redacted live/downstream proof before merge.

options.title: Fold Into Broader RFC
options.body: Pause or close this branch and handle token counts together with the provenance/internal-event assemble metadata design.

options.title: Keep Helpers Private For Now
options.body: Avoid new SDK runtime exports until maintainers settle the stable plugin-facing API shape.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Contract After Proof
recommendation.body: Approve `currentTokenCount` as a standalone assemble signal, then require SDK baseline regeneration and redacted live/downstream proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to this PR and have the strongest recent history on context-engine budgeting and Codex projection paths.
